secondary.note: born under the law to redeem

event_birth_of_jesus.notes: The birth of Christ fulfills centuries of prophetic expectation. Shepherds witness the glory; angels announce peace; the Messiah enters the world in humility.

event_jesus_baptism.notes: The heavens open, the Spirit descends, and the Father declares Jesus as His beloved Son. This is the formal divine commissioning of Jesus’ messianic mission.

event_first_disciples_called.title: First disciples called
event_first_disciples_called.notes: Jesus calls fishermen, tax collectors, and ordinary people to follow Him. Their calling marks the formation of the new covenant community and the beginning of the kingdom movement.

event_sermon_on_the_mount.title: Sermon on the Mount

detail.detail: judged to say the same thing (DeepSeek Flash)

secondary.label: James 1–3
secondary.note: wisdom and ethics echo Jesus’ teaching

event_sermon_on_the_mount.notes: Jesus reveals the ethics of the kingdom: beatitudes, deeper righteousness, love of enemies, prayer, trust, and wise living. It is the constitution of the new covenant people.

event_centurions_servant_healed.title: Centurion’s servant healed
event_centurions_servant_healed.notes: The centurion displays extraordinary faith, recognizing Jesus’ authority to heal with a word. Jesus marvels and declares that many Gentiles will enter the kingdom.

event_calming_the_storm.title: Calming the storm
event_calming_the_storm.notes: Jesus rebukes wind and waves with divine authority. The disciples ask, “Who is this?” — a key revelation moment showing Jesus as Lord over creation.

event_gerasene_demoniac.title: Gerasene demoniac
event_gerasene_demoniac.notes: Jesus confronts a legion of demons, liberates a man, and sends him as a witness to the Decapolis. This event displays cosmic authority and cross‑cultural mission.

event_raising_of_jairus_daughter.title: Raising of Jairus’ daughter
event_raising_of_jairus_daughter.notes: Jesus takes the girl by the hand and says, “Talitha koum.” She rises, demonstrating Jesus’ authority over death and foreshadowing His own resurrection.

event_woman_with_issue_of_blood.title: Woman with issue of blood
event_woman_with_issue_of_blood.notes: Her twelve‑year affliction ends instantly when she touches Jesus’ garment. Jesus affirms her faith and restores her socially, physically, and spiritually.

event_feeding_of_the_five_thousand.notes: Jesus multiplies loaves and fish, feeding thousands. This sign reveals Him as the new Moses providing true bread and inaugurates the Bread of Life discourse.

event_walking_on_water.title: Walking on water

secondary.label: Job 9:8
secondary.note: God “tramples the waves of the sea”

event_walking_on_water.notes: Jesus walks on the sea, revealing divine authority. Peter briefly joins Him, illustrating faith and frailty. The disciples worship, declaring, “Truly you are the Son of God.”

event_peters_confession.title: Peter’s confession

secondary.label: Isaiah 53
secondary.note: suffering Messiah — immediately connected in Jesus’ teaching

event_peters_confession.notes: Peter declares, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Jesus affirms the confession as divinely revealed and speaks of the church’s future authority.

event_transfiguration.title: Transfiguration
event_transfiguration.notes: Jesus’ face shines like the sun; Moses and Elijah appear, representing Law and Prophets. The Father declares, “This is my beloved Son; listen to Him.” A preview of resurrection glory and the coming kingdom.

event_rich_young_ruler.title: Rich young ruler
event_rich_young_ruler.notes: The ruler seeks eternal life but cannot part with his wealth. Jesus teaches that entering the kingdom requires wholehearted allegiance — and that salvation is impossible apart from God’s power.

secondary.label: Zechariah 9:9
secondary.note: king comes humble on a donkey

event_triumphal_entry.notes: Jesus enters Jerusalem as the peaceful king, fulfilling prophecy. Crowds acclaim Him, but He weeps over the city’s coming judgment. This event initiates Passion Week.

event_gethsemane.title: Gethsemane
event_gethsemane.notes: Jesus wrestles with the Father’s will, sweating like blood. He embraces the cup — symbolizing divine judgment — and chooses obedience unto death. The disciples sleep; Jesus stands alone.

event_jesus_arrested.title: Jesus arrested
event_jesus_arrested.notes: Judas betrays Jesus with a kiss. Jesus stops Peter’s sword, heals the servant’s ear, and willingly submits. The disciples flee, fulfilling Scripture.

event_jesus_tried.title: Jesus tried
event_jesus_tried.notes: Jesus faces multiple illegal trials: before the Sanhedrin, Herod, and Pilate. False witnesses contradict themselves. Pilate declares Him innocent yet condemns Him under pressure. Jesus affirms His identity as Messiah and Son of Man.

event_crucifixion.title: Crucifixion

secondary.label: Zechariah 12:10
secondary.note: look on Him whom they pierced

event_crucifixion.notes: Jesus is crucified outside the city. Darkness covers the land. He forgives His executioners, promises paradise to the thief, and entrusts His mother to John. The temple veil tears, symbolizing new access to God. His death accomplishes redemption and defeats the powers.

event_burial.title: Burial

secondary.label: Isaiah 53:9
secondary.note: “with a rich man in his death”

secondary.label: Psalm 16:10
secondary.note: Holy One not abandoned to decay

secondary.label: 1 Corinthians 15:3–4
secondary.note: burial as part of gospel core

event_burial.notes: Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus bury Jesus in a new tomb. Women witness the burial. The sealed tomb and Roman guard emphasize the reality of His death and the impossibility of human tampering.

event_resurrection.title: Resurrection

mthemes.title: Father, Son And Holy Spirit (the Trinity)

secondary.label: John 20:29
secondary.note: “blessed are those who have not seen”

event_resurrection.notes: Jesus rises bodily on the third day. Women are first witnesses. Angels announce victory. The resurrection inaugurates new creation and confirms Jesus as the true King and Son of God.

event_great_commission.title: Great Commission

mthemes.title: Father, Son And Holy Spirit (the Trinity)

event_great_commission.notes: Jesus declares all authority in heaven and earth. He commands His disciples to make disciples of all nations, baptizing and teaching. His final promise: “I am with you always.”

event_boy_jesus_in_the_temple.title: Boy Jesus in the temple

within.title: The Boy Jesus at the Temple

secondary.label: Malachi 3:1
secondary.note: Lord comes to His temple — early foreshadow

event_boy_jesus_in_the_temple.notes: At age twelve, Jesus demonstrates unique wisdom and awareness of His divine mission: “Did you not know I must be in my Father’s house?” This anticipates His later temple ministry.

event_good_samaritan.title: Good Samaritan

within.title: The Parable of the Good Samaritan

event_good_samaritan.notes: Jesus redefines “neighbor” through a shocking reversal: the outsider shows true covenant love. The parable exposes legalistic self‑justification and reveals the kingdom ethic of sacrificial mercy.

within.title: The Parable of the Rich Fool
The Parable of the Lost Coin

event_prodigal_son.title: Prodigal Son

within.title: The Parable of the Prodigal Son

event_prodigal_son.notes: The younger son’s rebellion and return reveal the heart of the Father — running, embracing, restoring. The older brother exposes self‑righteousness. The parable is the gospel in narrative form.

event_road_to_emmaus.title: Road to Emmaus
event_road_to_emmaus.notes: Jesus walks with two disciples, opens the Scriptures, and reveals how the Law, Prophets, and Writings point to Him. Their hearts burn as He teaches. Recognition comes in the breaking of bread.

event_ascension.title: Ascension

mthemes.title: Father, Son And Holy Spirit (the Trinity)

event_ascension.notes: Jesus ascends bodily, enthroned at the Father’s right hand. Angels promise His return. The ascension marks the beginning of His heavenly reign and the church’s mission.

event_first_miracle_at_cana.title: First miracle at Cana
event_first_miracle_at_cana.notes: Turning water into wine reveals Jesus’ glory and signals the arrival of new creation joy. It also foreshadows the messianic wedding feast and the transformation Jesus brings.

event_nicodemus_conversation.title: Nicodemus conversation
event_nicodemus_conversation.notes: Jesus teaches that entrance into the kingdom requires being “born of water and Spirit.” The conversation culminates in the declaration of God’s love and the Son’s mission.

event_samaritan_woman.title: Samaritan woman
event_samaritan_woman.notes: Jesus crosses ethnic, moral, and religious boundaries to reveal Himself as Messiah. The woman becomes a witness, and many Samaritans believe — a foretaste of global mission.

event_bread_of_life_discourse.title: Bread of Life discourse
event_bread_of_life_discourse.notes: After feeding the 5,000, Jesus interprets the sign: He Himself is the true bread from heaven. Eating His flesh and drinking His blood points to deep union with Him through faith.

within.title: Jesus Heals the Man Born Blind

event_raising_of_lazarus.title: Raising of Lazarus
event_raising_of_lazarus.notes: Jesus declares, “I am the resurrection and the life,” then proves it by calling Lazarus from the tomb. This sign precipitates the final conflict leading to the cross.

event_pentecost.title: Pentecost

parallels.label: Joel 2:28–32
parallels.section: I Will Pour Out My Spirit

secondary.label: Joel 2:28–32
secondary.note: Spirit poured out on all flesh

event_pentecost.notes: The Spirit descends with wind and fire. The apostles proclaim Jesus in many languages. Three thousand believe. Pentecost is the birth of the church and the fulfillment of prophetic promises.

event_healing_of_the_lame_man.title: Healing of the lame man
event_healing_of_the_lame_man.notes: Peter and John heal a man lame from birth. The miracle draws crowds and leads to gospel proclamation. It demonstrates the risen Christ’s ongoing power through His apostles.

event_philip_and_the_ethiopian_eunuch.title: Philip and the Ethiopian eunuch
event_philip_and_the_ethiopian_eunuch.notes: Philip explains Isaiah 53, proclaiming Jesus. The eunuch believes and is baptized, becoming the first recorded fully Gentile convert. This event previews the global reach of the gospel.

event_sauls_conversion.notes: Saul, persecutor of the church, encounters the risen Christ on the road to Damascus. He is blinded, healed, baptized, and commissioned as apostle to the Gentiles. His conversion is a paradigm of grace and mission.

event_cornelius.notes: Cornelius, a Roman centurion, receives a vision. Peter receives a vision of clean and unclean animals. The Spirit falls on Gentiles, demonstrating full inclusion without circumcision. This event is a watershed moment in salvation history.

event_pauls_missionary_journeys.notes: Paul and his companions proclaim Christ across Asia Minor and Greece. Churches are planted, elders appointed, miracles performed, and Scripture taught. The gospel spreads through synagogues, marketplaces, homes, and courts.

event_jerusalem_council.title: Jerusalem Council
event_jerusalem_council.notes: A major dispute arises: must Gentiles be circumcised? The apostles and elders gather. Peter, Paul, and James affirm salvation by grace through faith. Gentiles are welcomed without becoming Jews. This decision preserves gospel unity and fuels mission.

event_philippi_imprisonment_and_delivera.title: Philippi imprisonment and deliverance

secondary.label: Philippians 1:12–14
secondary.note: Paul reflects on imprisonment advancing the gospel

event_philippi_imprisonment_and_delivera.notes: Paul and Silas are beaten and imprisoned. They pray and sing hymns at midnight. An earthquake opens the doors; the jailer is converted and baptized. This event reveals God’s power to turn suffering into salvation.

event_paul_before_felix.title: Paul before Felix

secondary.label: 2 Timothy 4:16–17
secondary.note: Lord stands by Paul in trials

event_paul_before_felix.notes: Paul defends himself against false accusations. Felix is intrigued but corrupt, hoping for a bribe. Paul speaks boldly about righteousness, self‑control, and the coming judgment — unsettling Felix. Paul remains imprisoned for two years, yet his witness continues.

event_paul_before_festus_and_agrippa.title: Paul before Festus and Agrippa

secondary.label: Acts 9:15
secondary.note: Paul will bear Christ’s name before kings

event_paul_before_festus_and_agrippa.notes: Paul recounts his conversion and proclaims the resurrection. Agrippa is almost persuaded. Festus calls Paul mad; Paul insists on truth and reason. Paul appeals to Caesar, setting the stage for his journey to Rome.

event_shipwreck_on_malta.title: Shipwreck on Malta
event_shipwreck_on_malta.notes: A violent storm threatens all aboard. Paul encourages the crew, declaring God’s promise of survival. The shipwreck leads to Malta, where Paul survives a viper bite and heals many. The event reveals God’s sovereignty and opens new mission doors.

event_paul_in_rome.title: Paul in Rome
event_paul_in_rome.notes: Paul arrives in Rome under house arrest. He proclaims the kingdom of God to Jews and Gentiles. Some believe; others reject. Acts ends with Paul preaching “with all boldness and without hindrance,” symbolizing the unstoppable spread of the gospel.

event_revelation_vision_on_patmos.notes: John, exiled on Patmos, receives a cosmic revelation: the risen Christ, the heavenly throne room, the Lamb’s victory, the fall of Babylon, and the new creation. Revelation unveils the true nature of history — Christ reigns, evil will fall, and God will dwell with His people forever.

parallels.section: Daniel’s Vision of the Four Beasts

secondary.label: Exodus
secondary.note: background for trumpet and bowl judgments

event_revelation_judgments.notes: Seals, trumpets, and bowls unveil God’s judgments against evil powers and rebellious nations. The dragon, beast, and false prophet oppose the Lamb but are defeated. Babylon falls. Satan is bound, released, and finally destroyed. These judgments reveal God’s justice and vindicate His people.

event_new_creation_consummation.title: New creation consummation

within.title: A New Heaven and a New Earth

parallels.label: Isaiah 65:17–25
parallels.section: A New Heaven and a New Earth

event_new_creation_consummation.notes: God makes all things new. The new Jerusalem descends. Death, mourning, and pain vanish. God dwells with His people; the Lamb is their light. The river of life and tree of life heal the nations. This is the final fulfillment of the biblical story — creation renewed, kingdom consummated, and eternal communion established.
